Definition: Whether primary laws, acts, or legal instruments exist that establish authority for cross-government data sharing and govern the data exchange system
Comments: Digital Code (Law No. 2017-20 of April 20, 2018) provides comprehensive legal framework for digital sector including data sharing, cybercrime, data protection and interoperability mandate. APDP (Personal Data Protection Authority) established. Decree No. 2022-324 (June 2022) merged 4 agencies into ASIN with clear mandates. Legal framework enforces interoperability.
revision_notes: All three originally cited sources were fetched and support the score: DLA Piper confirms Law No. 2017-20 (Digital Code, amended 2020-35) and Law No. 2009-09 govern personal data processing; the Include Platform paper documents Benin's legal/institutional digital reforms since 2016; the 2025 Biometric Update article confirms ASIN operates a UXP (X-Road-based) interoperability platform under 'robust legal frameworks that enforce interoperability', with 1,500+ services and 55+ institutions connected. A targeted search additionally located the primary legal texts: Decret No. 2022-324 (1 June 2022, sgg.gouv.bj) creating ASIN by merging four digital agencies, and Decret No. 2020-209 (18 March 2020) establishing Benin's official 'Cadre d'interoperabilite' (interoperability framework), which is the most directly on-point legal instrument for this variable. Score of 3 (Yes) is well supported by multiple authoritative, primary legal sources; confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Benin's cross-government data-sharing authority rests on a layered legal framework: the Digital Code (Law No. 2017-20 of 20 April 2018, amended by Law No. 2020-35) sets the overarching legal basis for data processing and interoperability; Decree No. 2020-209 of 18 March 2020 establishes the national Cadre d'interoperabilite (interoperability framework) governing data exchange between public administrations; and Decree No. 2022-324 of 1 June 2022 creates the Agence des Systemes d'Information et du Numerique (ASIN) by merging four digital agencies, giving it a clear legal mandate to operate the interoperability platform. ASIN operates an Estonia-inspired X-Road/UXP-based data exchange system connecting over 55 institutions and more than 1,500 digitised services, underpinned by these legal instruments.
